nodes.label: Skeleton
nodes.rationale: Used for placeholder layouts that match the shape of asynchronously loaded content, including loading states in the Classes page while data is fetched.

nodes.label: App.useApp
nodes.rationale: Recommended for simple confirmation dialogs and for avoiding manual contextHolder implantation.

nodes.label: Modal.confirm
nodes.rationale: onOk/onCancel may return a promise; resolve closes the dialog and reject keeps it open, which delays closing until asynchronous work finishes.

nodes.label: Modal.destroyAll
nodes.rationale: Destroys all confirmation modals at once, typically on router change where keeping a reference to each dialog is impractical.

nodes.label: Modal.method
nodes.rationale: Static methods cannot consume ConfigProvider context and may cause style errors when the layer option is enabled.

nodes.label: Modal.useModal
nodes.rationale: Returns a modal instance and a contextHolder which must be placed under the context the modal should access; only the hooks method supports awaiting confirm().

nodes.label: DebounceSelect
nodes.rationale: Example pattern for remote search: lodash debounce plus a fetch id ref discards out-of-order responses while a small Spin signals the loading state.

nodes.label: popupRender
nodes.rationale: Custom dropdown content must stop MouseDown propagation or control the open prop to prevent the dropdown closing when losing focus.

nodes.label: showSearch
nodes.rationale: An array of optionFilterProp values searches multiple fields with OR matching; a custom filterOption overrides the default filtering logic.

nodes.label: tagRender
nodes.rationale: Preventing MouseDown propagation on a custom close icon stops the dropdown from reopening after the tag is removed.

nodes.label: virtual scroll
nodes.rationale: Enabled by default for better performance with large option lists; virtual={false} disables it so screen readers bind aria attributes to real elements instead of a mock node.

nodes.label: Space.Addon
nodes.rationale: Available since antd 5.29.0 for creating custom cells in compact layouts.

nodes.label: Space.Compact
nodes.rationale: Used when child form components are connected compactly with collapsed borders; supports Button, Select, Input and other form controls.

nodes.label: fullscreen
nodes.rationale: Adds a dimmed overlay with a centred spinner, suited to page loaders.

nodes.label: Spin.setDefaultIndicator
nodes.rationale: Defines a default spin element globally.

nodes.label: Tag.CheckableTag
nodes.rationale: A selectable tag controlled by checked and onChange.

nodes.label: Tag.CheckableTagGroup
nodes.rationale: Groups multiple checkable tags and reports the selected values together.

nodes.label: ConfigProvider tooltip.unique
nodes.rationale: With unique set to true only one Tooltip under the ConfigProvider is displayed at a time; getContainer and arrow are then ignored.

nodes.label: Tooltip fresh
nodes.rationale: Forces content updates while the Tooltip is closed instead of using the cached content.

nodes.label: Modal
nodes.rationale: Static Modal.method calls create a separate React instance via ReactDOM.render and cannot consume context; the hooks version or an App-provided instance is preferred when context access or layered styling matters.

nodes.label: Select
nodes.rationale: A dropdown menu for displaying choices; Radio is recommended when there are fewer than five options and AutoComplete when users should be able to type as well as select.

nodes.label: Space
nodes.rationale: Adds a wrapper around each child for inline alignment; Flex is preferred for block-level layout because it adds no wrapper and offers more control.

nodes.label: Spin
nodes.rationale: A loading animation for parts of a page waiting on asynchronous data or rendering; small for text, default for a card-level block and large for a page.

nodes.label: Tag
nodes.rationale: Used for tagging by dimension or property, categorising, highlighting important information and displaying status.

nodes.label: Tooltip
nodes.rationale: Caches content while closed to avoid flicker when content changes; set fresh to update content while closed. Child elements must accept mouse and focus events for the HOC to work.

nodes.label: Collapse accordion mode
nodes.rationale: accordion restricts expansion to one panel at a time; otherwise any number of panels may be open, with defaultActiveKey setting the initial panel.

nodes.label: Collapse ItemType
nodes.rationale: Items (preferred over the deprecated Collapse.Panel since 5.6.0) carry key, label, children, extra, collapsible, forceRender, showArrow and semantic classNames/styles.

nodes.label: Collapse collapsible trigger
nodes.rationale: collapsible selects header, icon or disabled as the trigger area; showArrow={false} hides the arrow and cannot be combined with collapsible="icon".

nodes.label: Button color and variant system
nodes.rationale: type is syntactic sugar for color and variant mappings (e.g. type="primary" equals color="primary" variant="solid"); color and variant take precedence when both are supplied, and preset colours extend the palette.

nodes.label: Button types (primary/default/dashed/text/link)
nodes.rationale: Five button types cover main, ordinary, additive, secondary and external-link actions, with danger, ghost, disabled and loading as additional properties; the recommended property order is type -> shape -> size -> loading -> disabled.

nodes.label: Button size convention
nodes.rationale: Buttons support large, medium (the default when size is omitted) and small sizes, with token paddingInline 15px medium / 7px small.

nodes.label: Card sizes (medium/small)
nodes.rationale: Card supports medium (default) and small sizes with bodyPadding 24/12 and headerPadding 24/12 tokens respectively; small is used for dense list/grid data cards, medium for standalone panels.

nodes.label: Alert closable configuration
nodes.rationale: closable accepts a boolean or a ClosableType with closeIcon, onClose and afterClose; top-level afterClose/onClose/message/closeText are deprecated in favour of their closable.* or title equivalents.

nodes.label: Alert.ErrorBoundary
nodes.rationale: Alert.ErrorBoundary wraps children to catch rendering errors, rendering title (default {{ error }}) and description (default {{ error stack }}).

nodes.label: Alert types (success, info, warning, error)
nodes.rationale: Alert displays persistent messages requiring attention with four types; type defaults to info, or warning in banner mode, and the variant prop (outlined/filled, default outlined) controls styling.

nodes.label: Card.Grid
nodes.rationale: Card.Grid lays out grid-style card content with hoverable defaulting to true.

nodes.label: Card.Meta
nodes.rationale: Card.Meta supplies avatar, title and description for flexible card content.

nodes.rationale: The template appsscript.json must carry the same oauthScopes and enabledAdvancedServices as the Admin Sheet to prevent permission errors for some users.

nodes.norm_label: script authorisation and trigger installation flow
nodes.rationale: First-run initialisation must consistently prompt for and validate the required scopes across users.

nodes.label: Per-user script authorisation verification
nodes.rationale: An administrative authorisation must not falsely mark other users as authorised.

nodes.label: authUsers double serialisation
nodes.rationale: authUsers is a JSON string whose content is a JSON array; un-escaping or double-escaping the manual seed makes the strict resolver deny access.

nodes.label: Fresh-install bootstrap claim
nodes.rationale: The first eligible interactive caller becomes sole administrator through an atomic, lock-guarded claim; trigger execution and blank identities never claim.

nodes.label: Authentication deploy-order contract
nodes.rationale: apiAuth transport and dispatcher admission ship together, and the backend-config and frontend Zod field removals ship together; a single clasp push prevents half-deployed shapes.

nodes.label: Two-provider authentication model
nodes.rationale: Retain the Google Group gate as one provider and add a Script Properties provider for named users; the removed 'none' mode is rejected fail-closed.

nodes.label: GAS Web App deployment (v1)
nodes.rationale: Deploy once as a web app instead of copying into a bound spreadsheet script; it runs as the signed-in user within a Google Workspace domain.

nodes.label: Zero-weight score reporting
nodes.rationale: Zero-weight tasks stay visible but are excluded from aggregate averages, with the interface identifying excluded scores.

nodes.label: Baseline task analysis (Averages basis)
nodes.rationale: Average against tasks attempted by the top 10% most-engaged students (minimum two) so a task skipped by the whole class does not drag the average down.

nodes.label: ABClass validated metadata snapshot
nodes.rationale: A durable post-analysis summary of class-wide averages and recent assignments gives later visualisations data to draw on.

nodes.label: Inline Source unavailable alert
nodes.rationale: Known errors no longer collapse the whole preview into a loading or generic failure state, and recorded reasoning stays visible.

nodes.label: Bootstrap mode for empty group email
nodes.norm_label: bootstrap mode for empty group email
nodes.rationale: Anyone in the Workspace domain gets access while the group email is empty so the first administrator can reach Settings.

nodes.label: TDD-first workflow (Red, Green, Refactor)
nodes.rationale: Each section completes red and green loops independently; the expensive regression checker runs once per completed section, not between phases, to preserve signal while controlling cost.

nodes.label: E2E test routing
nodes.rationale: Playwright owns browser E2E work because the Testing Specialist covers only Vitest unit/component and backend tests.

nodes.label: Same-Change Documentation Obligation
nodes.rationale: Detailed policy lives in owning docs and AGENTS files only route to them, so guidance has one source of truth.

nodes.label: Assignment definition reuse by title, topic and year group
nodes.norm_label: assignment definition reuse by title, topic and year group

nodes.label: Inform teacher judgement principle
nodes.rationale: Assessment Bot informs teacher judgement and deliberately does not feed information back to students; the teacher decides how to deliver feedback.

nodes.label: LLM-generated feedback limitation
nodes.rationale: Generating genuinely helpful per-student feedback is hard and time-consuming, and the extra context needed for each learner cannot practically be supplied to an LLM for any number of students.

nodes.label: Deferred cleanup trigger (Section 4)
nodes.rationale: One trigger per user with terminal-only deletion and re-arming keeps cleanup off the request path and never removes a record whose run may still be in flight.

nodes.label: Keyed ProgressTracker store and active run context (Section 2)
nodes.norm_label: keyed progresstracker store and active run context (section 2)
nodes.rationale: Per-run keyed records avoid parallel runs overwriting one another while the active context keeps existing call sites signature-free.

nodes.label: Keyed progress records
nodes.rationale: Separate per-run User Properties avoid the read-modify-write contention of a single shared blob and allow one getProperties scan for a status poll.

nodes.label: Frontend API surface only (no polling)
nodes.rationale: Polling scheduling and hooks are explicitly out of scope so this feature changes no visible UI.

nodes.label: skipTooManyTriggersRecovery option
nodes.rationale: Under this option a full trigger quota must not call removeTriggers, which would delete unrelated assessment triggers.

nodes.label: Sort order (timestamp then requestId)
nodes.rationale: The requestId tie-break makes the getProgress payload deterministic for consumers.

nodes.label: Bespoke NodeJS assessment backend
nodes.rationale: Replaced Langflow because the lightweight NodeJS service has a tiny footprint, faster request handling, fewer build/runtime errors and a simpler debugging surface.

nodes.label: Canonical UTC DateTime Predicate (Validate.isCanonicalUtcDateTime)
nodes.rationale: Enforces exact YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ form for metadata domain validation; the transport's isIsoDateTimeString_ accepts timezone offsets and is not used by the model domain.

nodes.label: LLMSeedPhase Partition and Batch Consumer
nodes.rationale: partitionRequests takes the first eligible request per taskDefinition as a seed; createBatchConsumer is the single onBatchComplete consumer shared by both phases, consuming each UID exactly once.

nodes.label: ABClassPersistence Prepared Writes
nodes.rationale: Full and partial payloads are prepared before the first mutation and written full first; vendor matchedCount checking makes an _id-only no-op patch count as a match.

nodes.label: Response Mapper Reuse and Stored-Read Date Revival
nodes.norm_label: response mapper reuse and stored-read date revival
nodes.rationale: One stored-partial metadata gate serves registry reads and mutation summaries; JsonDbApp revives ISO strings as Date objects, so stored-read gates convert them back before domain validation.

nodes.label: Trailing-Underscore Shared Helpers
nodes.rationale: Transport helpers are trailing-underscore functions whose JSDoc owns their signatures; domain validators live with their owning class or controller.

nodes.label: API Layer Tests
nodes.rationale: API-layer tests target src/backend/z_Api and cover thin boundary wrappers: correct controller delegation, required parameters and fail-fast error propagation; deep business logic stays in controller and service suites.

nodes.label: Backend API Layer (z_Api)
nodes.rationale: The sole backend transport owner for frontend-callable methods invoked through apiHandler, organised as REST-ish domain API surfaces.

nodes.label: Controller Request Gate (_validateRequestMetadata)
nodes.rationale: An Object.hasOwn check means actual omission does nothing while explicit undefined fails; the gate runs before any read, roster refresh or write so invalid request metadata has no side effect.

nodes.label: Canonical Data-Shape Specification Obligation
nodes.rationale: Before changing any API method, schema, transport shape or persistence model, the relevant data-shape spec must be read and updated in the same change; contracts must never be changed from assumptions about the docs.

nodes.label: API Layer Design Rules
nodes.rationale: Keep API functions thin, delegate to controllers, validate transport inputs and fail fast, and keep allowlisted method names stable once frontend callers use them.

nodes.label: ABClassMetadata Domain Model
nodes.rationale: The constructor owns the nullable field's null default and returns defensive snapshots; runtime references to dependencies resolve only inside method bodies because this file sorts before Assessment and ABClassMetadataStandings in the concatenated GAS load order.

nodes.label: ABClassMetadataValidationError
nodes.rationale: A typed domain error with fieldPath that defaults to model provenance; only the controller's request-validation invocation tags it with inputSource: 'request', so the domain layer never throws transport errors.

nodes.label: Non-Callable Transport Helper Pattern
nodes.rationale: A trailing underscore excludes helpers from google.script.run, so no IIFE or namespace wrapper is needed; a guarded module.exports block exposes them to Node tests.

nodes.label: Transport Error Adaptation (adaptMetadataRequestError_)
nodes.rationale: Converts only request-tagged ABClassMetadataValidationError into ApiValidationError without logging; all other errors rethrow with original identity so integrity failures keep returning INTERNAL_ERROR.

nodes.label: BaseRequestManager Batch Transport
nodes.rationale: Sole HTTP dispatch and retry owner for LLM and image requests: at most three dispatches per request with 5s and 7.5s waits, retrying only network errors, HTTP 429 and 5xx sequentially per member.

nodes.label: LLM Assessment and Cache Identity
nodes.rationale: The cache key is a versioned hash of v1, task type and reference/template/student content hashes; only validated numeric results are cached and hits are re-validated before use.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Seed/Remainder LLM Dispatch
nodes.rationale: One seed request per taskDefinition is dispatched as a single parallel round before the remainder with the configured batch size; this adds one LLM round-trip and a shared batch consumer routes all outcomes.

nodes.norm_label: trigger auth with cache bypass and never-claim

nodes.label: OAuth scope minimisation
nodes.rationale: Readonly Classroom variants were tightened in v0.7.7 to match the read-only permissions the script actually needs; scopes should be added only when the code genuinely requires them and trigger scopes must stay in lockstep with the manifest.

nodes.label: Defence in depth
nodes.rationale: The GAS platform is the primary control and is sufficient when configured correctly; the application auth gate, attack-surface reduction and data-handling discipline exist because misconfiguration happens, the deployed surface is larger than the UI, and data should not exist where it does not have to.

nodes.label: Four-layer security model
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 is the primary control; layers 2-4 are complementary compensating controls rather than replacements for correct platform configuration.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record Rules
nodes.rationale: An ADR records context, alternatives and the decision with rationale, but must not contain delivery narrative, implementation status or change history.

nodes.label: Periodic Documentation Audit Scope
nodes.rationale: Release-note content, docs/plans and the Ant Design docs cache are excluded from audits, while ADRs are judged against ADR rules rather than the general delivery-narrative rule.

nodes.label: Bulk Progress Modal Click Race (Ant Design v6)
nodes.norm_label: bulk progress modal click race (ant design v6)
nodes.rationale: The rc-dialog entrance animation can swallow a confirmation click; clickModalConfirmAndDismiss waits for enablement and retries only while the dialog is genuinely open.

nodes.label: Geometry Assertion Flake (Ant Design v6)
nodes.rationale: Ant Design v6 causes a 21-68px offset between the year-group button and table wrapper; ALIGNMENT_TOLERANCE_PX is 72px and still insufficient across Chromium versions and rendering modes.

nodes.label: Choose the Doc Action
nodes.rationale: Maps a change to none, wording correction, tutorial edit, a short section at the decision point, a new tutorial or an explainer; find the owning doc first and extend it rather than write a rival.

nodes.label: Journey Inventory
nodes.rationale: Each tutorial gets its own folder with index.md and an images/ folder whose filenames are prefixed with the journey name; MkDocs treats index.md as the folder page.

nodes.label: Documentation Style Guide
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for writing Markdown under docs/ and agent instruction files; agent instruction files link here rather than repeating the rules.

nodes.label: Known Flaky Tests
nodes.rationale: Catalogues e2e tests with known flake patterns and their mitigations; these tests do not block feature development and are addressed in separate cleanup work.

nodes.label: Teacher Documentation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Decides when a teacher-facing tutorial or explainer is needed and how the implementer, Docs agent and Playwright agent produce one.

nodes.label: Assessment Bot Documentation Index
nodes.rationale: Top-level navigation index linking teacher how-tos, setup, pedagogy, developer docs, architecture ADRs, security, release notes and templates.

nodes.label: Audience and Writing Style Matrix
nodes.rationale: Three audiences are served: teachers get one action or decision per step, developers get concise project-specific prose, and agents get unambiguous imperative must/must-not language; the audience row wins over general tone guidance.

nodes.label: What a Canonical Doc Is For
nodes.norm_label: what a canonical doc is for
nodes.rationale: State rules and reasoning needed to act correctly and describe behaviour as it is now or planned to become, not the sequence of work that produced it; documented planned features are allowed if kept accurate.

nodes.label: Don't Duplicate Code or JSDoc
nodes.rationale: JSDoc owns a symbol's contract, so docs link to the symbol and document why a rule exists and how components fit together; a missing or wrong JSDoc should be corrected rather than compensated for in prose.

nodes.label: Ownership and Navigation
nodes.rationale: Each topic has one owning doc with the full statement, other docs link to it; mkdocs.yml, docs/README.md and files on disk must agree, and working artefacts stay out of the published site via exclude_docs.

nodes.label: Screenshot Capture Workflow
nodes.rationale: The Playwright agent captures to a scratch location but cannot write under docs/, so the Docs agent moves chosen PNGs into the tutorial's images folder and writes the prose.

nodes.label: Teacher Documentation Trigger
nodes.rationale: The trigger is a change to what a teacher sees, decides or does, not the size of the code change; new choices and vocabulary are the strongest signals.

nodes.label: Agreed Product Decisions for the Regression CLI
nodes.norm_label: agreed product decisions for the regression cli
nodes.rationale: Optional sessionId defaults to the Git branch name, baselines auto-create when missing, compare runs exit non-zero on regressions, and Playwright always uses a dedicated single-worker lane.

nodes.label: Comparison Categories: regressions, new-failures, fixes
nodes.rationale: ESLint new warnings and errors both count as regressions, Vitest/Playwright newly skipped tests count as regressions, and any execution error counts as a regression.

nodes.label: Data-Shape Docs Consistency Focus
nodes.rationale: Triggered by changes to data-shape docs, validation schemas, API contracts or persistence models; cross-references code against canonical specs and flags both undocumented schema changes and stale docs.

nodes.label: Parallel Review Focuses
nodes.rationale: Core focuses always run and optional focuses run only for layers in the diff; every focus is launched in a single message so they run in parallel, and sub-agents cannot spawn further sub-agents.

nodes.label: PR_REVIEW.md Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Agent items are pasted verbatim with file:line evidence and incidental findings kept in their own subsection so blocking PR issues can be distinguished from cleanup opportunities.

nodes.label: Assessment Flow Guiding Principles
nodes.rationale: Progressive hydration, two-tier persistence, cache-first assessment, fail-fast with one boundary log, singletons and factories, trigger decoupling and bounded batch transport shape the whole run.

nodes.label: Error-Boundary Standards
nodes.rationale: Never use empty catch blocks or catch-and-return without logging; log once at the boundary with context and preserve raw thrown values rather than reducing them to lossy strings.

nodes.label: New-Code Logging Policy
nodes.rationale: Log at meaningful boundaries with structured metadata and one canonical method name per request at every site, because normalising the name at only one site fragments log correlation.

nodes.label: Backend Test Anti-Patterns
nodes.rationale: Treat stale import paths, test fallbacks in runtime code, broken numbered-file references, action-plan-based test names and unrestored globals as regressions.

nodes.label: Backend Coverage Gate
nodes.rationale: Coverage thresholds must not be waived or lowered to make the aggregate green; the regression checker runs tests without coverage so it can pass while the coverage command fails.

nodes.label: Backend Test Import Routes
nodes.rationale: #backend/* loads CommonJS owners, #synthetic-data/* is ESM-only, #test-helpers/* resolves two or more parents up, and relative imports may traverse at most one parent.

nodes.label: Vitest Projects and Commands
nodes.rationale: Four projects are defined: node, synthetic-analysis, synthetic-analysis-stress and plugins, each with its own npm command.

nodes.label: Backend Testing
nodes.rationale: Vitest-in-Node guidance for GAS backend tests covering runtime model, layout, harness rules and conventions that keep suites meaningful without live GAS services.

nodes.label: Global Mock Management
nodes.rationale: Never use bare delete global.X in cleanup because deleting a global installed by setupGlobals.js pollutes later suites; use globalMockManager's withTemporaryGlobals or beforeEach/afterEach pair.

nodes.label: Production/Test Boundary
nodes.rationale: Production files stay GAS-first with only a guarded end-of-file export block; missing globals and prerequisites belong in tests/setupGlobals.js rather than guarded require calls in runtime files.

nodes.label: GAS Concatenation Runtime Model
nodes.rationale: GAS concatenates files in filename order, so numeric prefixes encode load order; files must not be renamed or renumbered merely to satisfy a test import.

nodes.label: Canonical Synthetic Fixtures Policy
nodes.rationale: New and newly touched tests must use deterministic corpus fixtures rather than hard-coded literals and derive expectations from them; loaded views are deeply frozen and must be cloned before mutation.

nodes.label: No durable client-side storage
nodes.rationale: A stolen or compromised client holds nothing recoverable after the browser closes; the cost is no offline cache and no instant re-render after reload.

nodes.label: HARD GATE: Validation Before Handoff
nodes.rationale: A task is successful only when no new errors or warnings appear; five bounded repair attempts are allowed before stopping.

nodes.label: Phase-Aware Validation Before Handoff
nodes.rationale: A truthful blocked or incomplete handoff is always required when work cannot finish; validation evidence must match the assigned phase.

nodes.label: HARD GATE: Validation Before Handoff
nodes.rationale: Work is not handed back until relevant lint, type and test checks pass with no new errors or warnings; five repair attempts are allowed.

nodes.label: Alternatives Considered in ADR-001
nodes.rationale: Dual-field runtime conversion was rejected because it perpetuates ambiguity, and model getters/setters were rejected as over-engineering beyond scope.

nodes.label: Assignment-Definition Upsert Validation Split
nodes.rationale: The transport helper owns request shape and safe identifiers while the controller owns topic membership, duplicate tuples, weighting rules and persistence; the transport never derives definitionKey.

nodes.label: ADR-001: Adopt yearGroupKey-only with Controller-Resolution Pattern
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: adopt yeargroupkey-only with controller-resolution pattern
nodes.rationale: Adopted on 2025-05-19 to remove assignment-definition creation debt: duplicated creation methods, ambiguity between yearGroup and yearGroupKey, defaulting in multiple layers and silently accepted deprecated parameters.

nodes.label: Controller-Resolution Pattern
nodes.rationale: Controllers accept yearGroupKey: string | null and resolve it to non-null before model calls, so the model constructor and fromJSON receive a non-null string and yearGroupLabel supplied by the controller.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast Deprecated Parameter Validation
nodes.rationale: The model throws TypeError when deprecated yearGroup is present so missed migration entries surface immediately instead of causing silent data corruption.

nodes.label: Single Canonical Reference: yearGroupKey
nodes.rationale: The string yearGroupKey is the only year-group reference in active code, giving one source of truth; definition keys embed it, for example Math_Algebra_year-group-10.

nodes.label: Validation Ownership in the ADR
nodes.rationale: Transport validation belongs to the API layer, domain validation to the controller and data defaults and integrity to the model; this separation prevents future ownership violations.

nodes.label: Validation Ownership Rules
nodes.rationale: Transport shape, identifier path-safety and foreign-API response shape checks belong in z_Api helpers; business invariants belong in controllers, and a duplicated rule must be an explicitly marked defence-in-depth guard.

nodes.label: ABClass Transport Endpoints
nodes.rationale: upsert, update, delete and read endpoints share the validateSafeTrimmedIdentifier_ boundary as a marked defence-in-depth guard; metadata is a whole-value replacement, never a nested patch.

nodes.label: Assessment Transport Endpoints
nodes.rationale: startAssessmentRun and getAssignment carry freshness and not-found semantics; getAssignment strips progressTracker and deep-converts dates at the boundary.

nodes.label: Backend Configuration Endpoints
nodes.rationale: getBackendConfig returns 12 non-auth fields with masked apiKey and seeds defaults on first read; setBackendConfig rejects auth fields for every caller and commits one merged patch.

nodes.label: Assignment-Definition Transport Endpoints
nodes.rationale: upsert, get, partial-list and delete endpoints share one canonical editable entity response shape so the frontend keeps a single model; updatedAt acts as a request-side concurrency token.

nodes.label: Reference-Data Transport Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Cohort, year-group and assignment-topic CRUD strips storage metadata; deleting a referenced topic raises reason IN_USE which maps to the standard IN_USE envelope.

nodes.label: Registered Transport Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Documents the allowlisted methods for configuration, ABClass, assignment definitions, assessment, classrooms and reference data, each with its source helper, request fields and frontend wrapper.

nodes.label: startAssessmentRun API Trigger
nodes.rationale: Validates definitionKey, assignmentId and courseId at the transport boundary, checks definition freshness via Drive modification times, resolves the ABClass and delegates to startProcessing.

nodes.label: Trigger Setup and Context Storage
nodes.rationale: Creates a five-second time-based trigger and stores the run context in Script Properties keyed by triggerUid so heavy work runs off-trigger and user-facing operations return quickly.

nodes.label: Admission Control and Tracking
nodes.rationale: A per-user lock with bounded timeout, stale-record pruning and ACTIVE_LIMIT enforcement records started/success/error lifecycle entries compacted to bounded metadata.

nodes.label: apiHandler Transport
nodes.rationale: The canonical transport entrypoint accepts a method and params and returns an INVALID_REQUEST envelope rather than throwing when the payload is invalid.

nodes.norm_label: transport error mapping and failure diagnostics
nodes.rationale: One boundary ABLogger.error entry with requestId and canonical method preserves developer diagnostics while the frontend envelope stays stable and free of stack traces.

nodes.label: Backend Error Type Inventory
nodes.rationale: Records each recognised error class, its path and where it is thrown; DefinitionStaleError and ClassNotFoundError carry structured metadata, and new types extend Error with a guarded module.exports block.

nodes.label: ALLOWLISTED_METHOD_HANDLERS Registry
nodes.rationale: The single authoritative registry: a method is reachable from the frontend if and only if it has an entry, and handler closures stay thin.

nodes.label: Node Test Bootstrap (setupGlobals.js)
nodes.rationale: Production files read concatenated-script globals with no require or globalThis assignments; Node tests mirror that layout by installing the same dependencies in tests/setupGlobals.js.

nodes.label: Prohibited Types in google.script.run
nodes.rationale: Date, Function and DOM elements are prohibited in both directions; the return direction is safe because apiHandler serialises to a JSON string, but a live Date in a request remains prohibited.

nodes.label: Response Envelope String Serialisation
nodes.rationale: apiHandler returns JSON.stringify of the envelope because google.script.run can drop null properties from objects; the frontend parses the string once and handlers must emit explicit null for absent nullable fields.

nodes.label: Assignment.create() Factory
nodes.rationale: Selects SlidesAssignment or SheetsAssignment from documentType; adding a document type requires a new subclass and a factory update.

nodes.label: Scoped Image Hydration
nodes.rationale: ImageManager collects, downloads and writes back images by scope; a pending student image with no source becomes that task's hydration E while a required shared image with no source throws.

nodes.label: processSelectedAssignment Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Receives dispatched params directly without reading User Properties, loads definition and class, creates the assignment, runs the pipeline, persists the run and counts failed items for completion feedback.

nodes.label: Assignment Processing Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Runs stages in sequence: add students, revalidate definition freshness, fetch submitted documents, extract work, hydrate images for Slides, assess responses and persist the run.

nodes.label: Sheets Formula Assessment
nodes.rationale: SheetsAssignment overrides assessResponses to use SheetsAssessor, which compares formulas cell by cell and produces completeness, accuracy and spag assessments plus transient cell-reference feedback.

nodes.label: Progressive Extraction and Artifact Materialisation
nodes.rationale: A failed-open sentinel creates per-task SOURCE_UNREADABLE items, a matched Slides IMAGE stays legitimately pending until hydration, and healthy items keep an empty assessment map until assessment.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Run Persistence
nodes.rationale: A completed-run gate mirrors marker-1 read invariants before any mutation, then the full record goes to assign_full_<courseId>_<assignmentId> and a partial summary into the class collection; the write order is non-transactional.

nodes.label: Trigger Execution and Cleanup
nodes.rationale: triggerHandler applies a fail-closed auth check with bypassCache and neverClaim, dispatches via TRIGGER_METHOD_HANDLERS and owns all context-clear and trigger deletion in a finally block.

nodes.label: Core principle - describe the current shape
nodes.norm_label: core principle - describe the current shape
nodes.rationale: Contract files describe what a boundary shape is today; status labels and delivery narrative never appear in them.

nodes.label: Self-update requirement for docs.md
nodes.rationale: The docs agent must update its own prompt when documentation files are added, removed or materially change so all agents know the current landscape.

nodes.label: Agent Modes: primary, subagent, all
nodes.rationale: V2 has three modes; a new custom agent defaults to primary, subagents run only in child sessions, and the default nesting depth of one means a subagent cannot launch a further subagent. V2 has no built-in scout agent.

nodes.label: Agent Configuration Locations (JSONC and Markdown)
nodes.rationale: Agents are defined either under the agents key in opencode.jsonc/json or as Markdown files; the filename stem becomes the agent name and a nested path becomes part of the agent ID.

nodes.label: Default Agent Selection
nodes.rationale: The selected default must exist, be visible and support primary use; otherwise OpenCode falls back to build and then the first visible primary-capable agent.

nodes.label: Agent Setup and Configuration Skill
nodes.rationale: Consults the official OpenCode Agents docs first; defines how V2 agents and subagents are created, configured and managed via JSONC config or Markdown files.

nodes.label: Agent Permissions (action, resource, effect)
nodes.rationale: Permissions are ordered rules where the last matching rule wins, so broad rules must be placed before exceptions; global rules apply before agent-specific rules and subagent launch can be restricted by subagent-action rules.

nodes.label: Backend File and Folder Organisation
nodes.rationale: Canonical rules for splitting oversized backend files and grouping z_Api transport files by domain.

nodes.label: ABClassController Facade Decomposition
nodes.rationale: A no-argument facade constructs injected owners and delegates without changing signatures; decomposition keeps the facade within the 500-line lint ceiling while preserving the public API.

nodes.label: API Domain Folder Organisation (z_Api)
nodes.rationale: Create a domain folder when at least two files share a leading lowercase prefix; keep single-file domains flat and update allowlist import paths and module.exports when nesting changes.

nodes.label: Large File Decomposition (Facade Pattern)
nodes.rationale: A non-API file above 550 lines must be split into a folder with an index.js facade and concern-named subclasses; the facade loads after subclasses, keeps the public API identical, and the threshold must not be gamed by reformatting or weakening JSDoc.

nodes.label: ClassPage no-data metric placeholder
nodes.rationale: The Class-page zero-data placeholder uses totalDataPoints: 0 because it represents a genuinely empty aggregate surface, unlike the heatmap not-attempted placeholder.

nodes.label: Imperative read with queryClient.query
nodes.rationale: When orchestration must await a shared read outside an observer, call queryClient.query: it resolves with the query function's data and rejects on failure so the caller can handle or log it. The deprecated fetchQuery and prefetchQuery methods must not be used for new code.

nodes.label: Invalidation-triggered background refetch pattern
nodes.rationale: Preferred pattern is to let invalidateQueries trigger React Query's automatic background refetch for active observers. An explicit queryClient.query after invalidation is an anti-pattern because its rejection is thrown at the call site and can be caught by the wrong scope (modal instead of page).

nodes.label: Query-key factory convention
nodes.rationale: Shared query keys are defined through queryKeys.ts factory helpers rather than ad-hoc array literals, so invalidation and warm-up work stays aligned to one source of truth.

nodes.label: Startup warm-up policy
nodes.rationale: Only slow, shared datasets (classPartials, assignmentDefinitionPartials, assignmentTopics, cohorts, yearGroups) are warmed after OAuth admission and application-access approval. Warm-up is fire-and-forget via queryClient.query with Promise.allSettled, is owned at an app-level boundary outside App.tsx, and never blocks the shell's initial render, paint or admission; failure is logged and published through StartupWarmupStateProvider.

nodes.rationale: A small Card with a type="default" back button on the left and right-aligned actions in declared order; wrapActions is opt-in (enabled only for the heatmap nav card), and a static Reassessment required tag appears for legacy assessmentContractVersion with no optimistic removal.

nodes.label: Two-card page header design
nodes.rationale: Each page level renders a PageTitleCard (title only) and a separate PageNavCard (back button plus right-aligned actions) so a child page can stack the parent's title without inheriting its actions; parent-level actions must not appear on the child page.

nodes.label: Region-by-Region User-Visible States
nodes.rationale: Each major region documents initial loading, ready, empty, warning and blocking-failure states, with data-heavy regions adding partial-load and stale-data rules.

nodes.label: Layout Spec Writing Rules
nodes.rationale: Keep the document UI-focused, move backend contracts to SPEC.md and sequencing to ACTION_PLAN.md, and state what is out of scope so the layout surface does not expand implicitly.

nodes.label: Frontend Layout Specification Template
nodes.rationale: Defines layout hierarchy, visible regions, component choices, workflow surfaces and user-visible states without drifting into backend contracts or delivery sequencing.

nodes.label: No Extra Navigation Layers

nodes.label: Spec Writing Rules

nodes.label: scc (Sloc, Cloc and Code) Binary
nodes.rationale: A direct binary download to ~/.local/bin is recommended because the apt package is not available on Debian or Ubuntu.

nodes.label: LOC Counter Skill
nodes.rationale: Counts lines of code and compares changes to verify LOC reduction, optimised for deduplication verification; run scc directly with the shell tool and keep bookkeeping in the scratchpad.

nodes.label: Baseline and Compare Actions
nodes.rationale: Re-extract a Git revision into a clean scratchpad directory before each comparison so stale files cannot inflate the before count; the scratchpad is gitignored and scc honours .gitignore by default.

nodes.rationale: The duplication endpoint returns block pairings with from and size, so a pair means lines [from, from+size) are duplicated between two file references.

nodes.label: Helper extraction decision rules
nodes.rationale: Keep logic local with one call site and no independent contract; extend when behaviour matches an existing responsibility; create only with two active call sites now or a documented near-term second site plus a coherent contract.

nodes.label: Reuse-first helper rule
nodes.rationale: Before creating a helper, identify the shared behaviour, check the canonical helper map, prefer extending an existing coherent helper, and create a new one only when none exists; never create a helper only to move code out of a large file.

nodes.label: CSS custom property spacing tokens
nodes.rationale: --app-spacing-xs/sm/md/lg/xl/xxl (4/8/16/24/32/48px) are the single source of truth for CSS and inline spacing; new CSS classes must reference them.

nodes.label: Theme-first reduced-motion source of truth
nodes.rationale: AppThemeShell listens to matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and drives the Ant Design token.motion (false when the OS requests reduced motion), with a CSS @media fallback zeroing sider transition duration/delay for when JavaScript media handling is unavailable or delayed.

nodes.label: Token-aligned CSS transitions
nodes.rationale: Shell CSS transitions consume Ant token values through custom properties --app-motion-duration-mid and --app-motion-ease-in-out rather than hard-coded easing or duration values.

nodes.label: Core Principles
nodes.rationale: Formatting is enforced by the linter; British English, KISS, fail-fast, no defaults and no scope creep are the rules it cannot catch.

nodes.label: Prefer rehydration over construction in backend tests
nodes.norm_label: prefer rehydration over construction in backend tests
nodes.rationale: Many GAS classes call live services in constructors, so fromJSON avoids constructor side effects in Node-based tests.

nodes.label: Availability by parent store and pending IMAGE
nodes.norm_label: availability by parent store and pending image
nodes.rationale: The definition store's pending-image state is internal and pre-run, never a terminal student E or N.

nodes.label: Partial JSON redaction of content and contentHash
nodes.norm_label: partial json redaction of content and contenthash
nodes.rationale: Content and contentHash are redacted in every partial projection so list views stay light; a null there is deliberate and never evidence of extraction failure.

nodes.label: Representation mode (full/partial) threading
nodes.rationale: Mode is threaded explicitly from the assignment root so partial redaction never triggers source-content failure detection or hash generation.

nodes.label: ClassSummaryAnalyser single owner
nodes.rationale: A dedicated analyser composes AveragingAnalyser and reuses its rollup helpers so no second averaging implementation is added outside the service.

nodes.label: Effective weighting (assignment x task weighting)
nodes.rationale: A null assignmentWeighting resolves to 1 before the product; a zero effective weight changes only average contribution, never the displayed score.

nodes.label: Dual display and contribution accumulation
nodes.rationale: Display evidence and average contribution are independent facts; a zero effective weight changes only the second, never turning an assessed numeric score into N or E.

nodes.label: Classroom vs assignment Zod strictness
nodes.rationale: Classrooms tolerate extra upstream fields while assignment responses reject unknown fields to catch accidental data leaks such as updateTime.

nodes.label: Deferred progress cleanup trigger
nodes.rationale: One deferred time-based trigger per user deletes terminal records only, with cache and marker dedupe so triggers are not duplicated.

nodes.label: ACTIVE_LIMIT concurrent request gate
nodes.rationale: ACTIVE_LIMIT leaves headroom below MAX_TRACKED_REQUESTS so completed entries do not trigger compaction on every request.

nodes.label: In-use protection on delete
nodes.rationale: Deletion is blocked when a partial references the key so the reference dataset cannot be corrupted by dangling references.

nodes.label: String transport via JSON.stringify
nodes.rationale: google.script.run can omit null properties from returned objects, so apiHandler returns a JSON string to preserve explicit null; an undefined property is still dropped by JSON.stringify.

nodes.label: Frontend serialisation boundary
nodes.rationale: dispatchAttempt is the sole JSON.parse choke point so feature code never handles raw GAS transport details.

nodes.label: Text button restriction
nodes.rationale: Button type="text" is permitted only for icon-only actions and header-inline shell toggles; labelled in-card actions must use the default or primary button so they carry Ant's standard paddingInline.

nodes.label: Card size convention
nodes.rationale: List/grid data cards use size="small" to stay compact while standalone settings/configuration panels use size="medium" (the Ant default). This is intentional, not an inconsistency; Ant component spacing defaults must not be overridden without documented UX justification.

nodes.label: Width-token ownership rules
nodes.rationale: Page and panel widths are owned by shared CSS custom properties rather than duplicated literals or ConfigProvider theme tokens.

nodes.label: Keep modal open on failure pattern
nodes.norm_label: keep modal open on failure pattern
nodes.rationale: A failed destructive confirmation stays open so the user can retry without reopening the modal.

nodes.label: React 19 StrictMode double-effect queue rule
nodes.rationale: StrictMode double-fires effects against the Vite dev server, so every response queue needs two entries per expected real call.

nodes.label: In-memory-only cache persistence policy
nodes.rationale: Frontend cache persistence is intentionally disabled so shared query payloads are never written to browser storage by default; cached data remains in memory for the current session because the app handles sensitive student-related data.

nodes.label: skipToken disabled-query pattern
nodes.rationale: An intentionally disabled useQuery should use skipToken as queryFn instead of a dummy async function returning an empty value; this makes the disabled intent explicit and removes the need for enabled: false.

nodes.label: ABClass metadata schema ownership
nodes.rationale: abClassMetadata.zod.ts is the single frontend owner of the ABClass wire metadata contract; ABClassMetadataSchema and NonNullableABClassMetadataSchema validate whole/nullable and complete snapshots with canonical UTC timestamps, dense zero-to-three recent entries and newest-first non-increasing timestamps, so consumers must not duplicate these rules.

nodes.label: ClassSummaryAnalyser
nodes.rationale: ClassSummaryAnalyser is the single owner of summary calculation, registered in its own DataAnalysisService field, composing AveragingAnalyser and reusing its exported rollupMetric, computeEffectiveWeight-adjacent helpers and convertToBaselineExcluded.

nodes.label: Breadcrumb extension for class detail
nodes.rationale: getBreadcrumbItems(key, className, onNavigateToClasses) builds the shell breadcrumb with no root segment; with a class detail open under 'classes' a clickable Classes segment is added, the final segment is non-clickable, and class name plus callback travel through ClassSelectionContext rather than duplicating page labels.

nodes.label: Centralised navigation metadata and page rendering
nodes.norm_label: centralised navigation metadata and page rendering
nodes.rationale: renderNavigationPage(...) in appNavigation.tsx is the single runtime source of truth for navigation-key-to-page rendering; AppShell consumes it rather than keeping a second page-selection switch, and menu items are memoised with useMemo over the smallest dependency set.

nodes.label: Mandatory apiHandler mock rule
nodes.rationale: Frontend tests mocking google.script.run.apiHandler must use createGoogleScriptRunApiHandlerMock in Vitest or inline googleScriptRunApiHandlerFactorySource in Playwright page.addInitScript; direct assignment to globalThis.google.script.run is prohibited so per-call callback isolation is preserved.

nodes.label: GAS serialisation fidelity rule
nodes.rationale: The harness passes strings unchanged (modelling the backend's serialised envelope), serialises objects once after dropping null object properties, rejects live Date values, leaves failureHandler unwrapped, and requires data: null for void/delete responses because JSON.stringify strips undefined.

nodes.label: Mandatory Playwright coverage for visible interactions
nodes.norm_label: mandatory playwright coverage for visible interactions
nodes.rationale: Every new or changed user-visible interaction (clicks, keyboard, tab switching, toggles, navigation) must have Playwright coverage; Vitest coverage alone is not sufficient for visible browser behaviour, and a browser journey must not drive weakened unit assertions.

nodes.label: Vitest/Playwright behaviour split
nodes.rationale: Vitest + Testing Library verify invisible behaviour and fast component logic (state transitions, callback wiring, conditional rendering, data/error mapping, accessibility attributes); Playwright verifies visible, real-browser behaviour and cross-page runtime integration. Default to Vitest first for fast feedback, then add Playwright for high-value journeys.

nodes.label: vi.resetAllMocks over vi.clearAllMocks
nodes.rationale: Use vi.resetAllMocks() in afterEach to reset both call history and implementations; vi.clearAllMocks() only clears history and leaves stale implementations. Globals installed with vi.stubGlobal must be paired with explicit vi.unstubAllGlobals().

nodes.label: Registration-only shared mock setup pattern
nodes.rationale: When several specs mock the same modules identically, use a module containing only imports and vi.mock calls that exports nothing, imported before the modules it mocks; each spec keeps its own isolation hooks and uses vi.resetAllMocks, without adding eslint-disable comments.

nodes.label: apiHandler sole transport entrypoint
nodes.rationale: All frontend requests route through the single ALLOWLISTED_METHOD_HANDLERS registry; parallel method-name registries are prohibited.

nodes.label: callApi sole frontend transport
nodes.rationale: All frontend-to-backend calls route through callApi; google.script.run and backend globals are prohibited transport shortcuts.

nodes.label: Singleton access via Class.getInstance()
nodes.rationale: Access singletons through getInstance() and never construct them directly.

nodes.label: Coding Principles
nodes.rationale: Defaults belong in constructors only, and nearby imports use relative paths while aliases are reserved for deeper traversals, so behaviour stays predictable across concatenated GAS code and Node tests.

nodes.label: Aggregate-only excluded state
nodes.rationale: excluded is valid only at aggregate scope; task displays keep numeric zero-weight scores and genuine raw N visible.

nodes.label: 550-line large file decomposition rule
nodes.rationale: Files over 550 lines must be split into coherent modules when in scope; formatting tricks that only lower the line count do not satisfy the rule.

nodes.label: Post-analysis metadata invalidation
nodes.rationale: postAnalysisInvalidation.ts completes confirmed metadata saves inside the shared hook's cached attempt, invalidating abClass(classId) and classPartials() each with throwOnError: true and awaiting both through Promise.allSettled so a failing detail refresh neither skips list invalidation nor hides its failure.

nodes.label: React Query shared server-state layer
nodes.rationale: React Query (@tanstack/react-query) is the single shared server-state layer for cache, freshness and in-flight request deduplication; no parallel cache layer is added for shared backend reads. Cache is in-memory for the current session and persistence is intentionally disabled because the app handles sensitive student data.

nodes.label: View-entry prefetch policy
nodes.rationale: Future features must pick one of startup prefetch, view-entry prefetch or on-demand loading; startup prefetch is reserved for slow shared datasets where the latency trade-off is justified, not to exercise React Query. ClassPage assignment warm-up (top 3) and Settings Google Classrooms prefetch are the current view-entry prefetches.

nodes.label: yearGroupKey/yearGroupLabel data contract
nodes.rationale: Assignment definitions store the selected authoritative yearGroupKey rather than a numeric yearGroup, with yearGroupLabel resolved for display from cached reference data; persisted records keep keys, not display values that may change.

nodes.label: Frontend abstraction anti-patterns to reject
nodes.rationale: Reject single-caller wrappers without independent contracts, duplicated orchestration skeletons, parallel derivation/preview/query paths beside an owner, duplicated routing render sources, mirrored validation-error stores and ad-hoc helper modules created without checking the canonical map.

nodes.label: Sequential FIFO API/local-task queue (apiQueue)
nodes.rationale: callApi, runApiQueuedTask, getQueueState and cancelApiQueued share one Map/Set registry with FIFO ordering per job name while different jobs run in parallel. A reserved slot covers the whole callback including awaited work; cancellation rejects pending entries with { reason: 'CANCELLED' }. Never await another enqueue on the same lane inside a task because it deadlocks, and network work uses callApi directly so callbacks never become GAS payloads.

nodes.label: Decorative icon wrapper convention
nodes.rationale: Navigation icon wrappers are decorative and hidden from assistive technology via aria-hidden on both the span.app-navigation-icon and the icon; tests prefer stable structural selectors (.app-navigation-icon in unit tests, Ant icon accessible labels in E2E) over inferred roles.

nodes.label: Canonical gap constants (theme/spacing.ts)
nodes.rationale: APP_GAP_XS/SM/COMPACT/MD/LG and APP_SPACE_SIZE_DEFAULT/TIGHT are the TypeScript-side source of truth for TSX gaps, mirroring the --app-spacing-* CSS tokens; magic-number gap/margin/padding literals must be replaced by them.

nodes.label: 8px spacing grid
nodes.rationale: Frontend spacing follows an 8px grid with small/middle/large = 8/16/24px, implemented in theme/spacing.ts and exposed as CSS custom properties; no value that is not a multiple of 8 is allowed except documented 4px exceptions.

nodes.label: 4px half-unit exception
nodes.rationale: The 4px (--app-spacing-xs) value is not part of Ant Design's standard scale and is permitted only for tight inner-element spacing such as filter-dropdown items, metric-pill compact mode and inline icon-to-text gaps; new uses require a documenting comment.

nodes.label: Canonical synthetic fixtures policy
nodes.rationale: New or changed tests must use the deterministic synthetic analysis corpus via the @synthetic/* alias when it covers the scenario, deriving expectations from corpus data; Vitest imports raw text with ?raw while Playwright imports parsed JSON without it.
